agree.reason: The signed training records, the two clean state audits and the GMP course with an end date give a skeptical HR manager concrete reasons to offer a phone screen, though leaving out the June 14 start date and interview availability could cost the call.

honest.reason: The letter drops the unsupported 'cut in half' claim, uses the true 20-to-12-hour reduction instead, and states the GMP gap plainly, though 'much of that work has been the job you're hiring for' goes a little beyond what the facts show.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are stated as given but not worked: the letter never calls the 20-to-12-hour change a 40% cut, never gives the 17-point (about 41% relative) rise in AP pass rate, and never counts the roughly 1,000+ students with signed safety records over the years.

right_comparison.reason: The before and after figures (20 vs 12 hours, 41% vs 58%) are fair, but the letter never sets the writer against the real alternative, a candidate who already has GMP experience, beyond admitting the gap.

qualification.reason: The GMP course has a checkable May 2 finish date, but the letter doesn't say when the writer could start (June 14) or what the reader gets when the course is done, such as a certificate.

objections.reason: It answers the 'teachers don't know regulated plants' doubt with audited, signed records and the course enrollment, but it leaves the start-date question open, and the reader will ask it.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter in the right form, but it uses a [Your Name] placeholder even though the name was known, and a stray '</invoke>' artifact is left at the end.
